excerpt: Two years ago, an admin panel for a simple website took me a day, maybe two - and I was proud of how fast I was. Now it takes me about... Two years ago, an admin panel for a simple website took me a day, maybe two - and I was proud of how fast I was. Now it takes me about an hour or two. The old day went like this. Install the package, generate the CRUDs, configure every field and column, wire up the relationships, click through everything to check it works. Thirty to sixty minutes per CRUD, easily. Now I describe what I want, the agent runs our generators, writes the configuration, writes the tests, and I review. A day of work fits in an hour. A week-long feature fits in a day. I'm not the only one seeing this. In February 2026, a customer from New Zealand gave us a 10 out of 10 in our feedback form. The whole review was one line: "Straightforward to use (particularly with Claude looking over my shoulder!)" That's the new normal. The developer isn't alone with the docs anymore. There's an agent next to them that already knows the package. I maintain Backpack for Laravel, an admin panel package that's been around for 10 years. We did a bunch of things to make the AI agents better at writing admin panels with Backpack - it's a quick-moving niche. But when I looked at why AI agents are so good at it, the answer surprised me. Most of it isn't the AI-specific stuff we built. Two of the things everyone tells you to add, llms.txt and an MCP server, barely helped us at all. Here's what did help, so you can do the same for your package. Let's get these out of the way first, because most "make your package AI-ready" advice starts with them. llms.txt. We shipped one. I don't think it does much. Agents rarely go looking for it. When they do, they find a table of contents for docs they could already read. Thinking of removing it, tbh. An MCP server.
